title: Compute Economics Playbook: initiative to reduce serving unit costs via batching, caching, and quantization
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective:
Create a repeatable, cross-functional playbook that drives at least 15–25% unit-cost reduction on typical Redwood inference workloads by standardizing experiments and rollout patterns for batching, KV/prefix caching, and quantization profiles. The playbook will include discovery templates, evaluation criteria, risk matrices, rollout runbooks, and dashboards for ongoing monitoring.

Scope:
- Define measurement baseline and UoM (cost per 1k tokens, p95 latency, tail SLA breaches) for hosted and Dedicated deployments.
- Establish canonical batching policies (static/auto/latency-targeted) and a testing harness for throughput vs latency trade-offs.
- Surface prefix/KV cache patterns, eviction policies, and recommended cache key schemas for common workloads (chat, summarization, embeddings).
- Validate quantization profiles across representative models (8-bit, 4-bit, mixed) with quality regression thresholds and rollback criteria.
- Produce rollout templates (canary, A/B, progressive traffic ramp) and feature-flag guidance.

Approach & trade-offs:
- Prioritize low-risk production levers first: caching and batching heuristics with conservative latency SLOs. Quantization will be gated behind an evaluation suite due to quality regressions risk.
- Balance implementation effort against expected unit-econ wins: initial emphasis on autoscaling-friendly batching and prefix caching for chat workloads, later expand to embeddings and reranking jobs.
- Recommended fallback strategy: if quality regressions exceed thresholds, route traffic to a non-quantized variant and trigger on-call paging.

Deliverables:
- Playbook doc in Confluence with experiment checklist and RBAC/upgrade notes.
- SDK-patterns and sample configs for SDK/CLI to enable per-route batching and cache policies.
- Evaluation harness (load + quality tests) and dashboards for cost, latency, and quality deltas.
- Three pilot rollouts across customer-facing workloads (hosted API chat, dedicated embeddings pipeline, private deploy demo).

Links to artifacts:
- Confluence (playbook draft): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/COGS/compute-economics-playbook
- Evaluation harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/compute-econ-eval
- Dashboard prototype: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/compute-econ/playbook-v1
- Design mock for rollout UI: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1Gplaybook-mock/view

Notes on governance:
- Playbook reviewed weekly with runtime, infra, DX, and applied-ML. Major changes require sign-off from Runtime Eng lead and Security. Rollouts that affect more than 5% of traffic need PM + Eng on-call in the loop.
acceptance_criteria: Baseline measurement established for hosted and Dedicated (cost/1k tokens, p95 latency, SLA breach rate) and validated against production samples
Canonical batching policy prototypes implemented in runtime and SDK, with public docs and a sample config
metrics: Unit cost (cost per 1k tokens) reduction goal: 15% minimum, 25% stretch on targeted workloads
No more than 5% increase in p95 latency for chat workloads during first pilot
Quality regression (measured by eval prompts) below 1.5% absolute for quantized models in pilot
Adoption: 3 pilot customers/teams complete playbook run by end of Q2
